In [[algebraic geometry]], an '''ideal sheaf''' (or '''sheaf of ideals''') is the global analogue of an [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] in a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]]. The ideal sheaves on a geometric object are closely connected to its subspaces.

== Definition ==

Let <math>X</math> be a [[topological space]] and <math>A</math> a [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] of rings on <math>X</math>; i.e., let <math>(X,A)</math> be a [[ringed space]]. An ideal sheaf <math>J</math> in <math>A</math> is a [[subobject]] of <math>A</math> in the [[category (mathematics)|category]] of sheaves of <math>A</math>-modules, i.e., a [[sheaf (mathematics)|subsheaf]] of <math>A</math> viewed as a sheaf of abelian groups such that
:<math>\Gamma(U,A)\cdot\Gamma(U,J)\subseteq \Gamma(U,J)</math>
for all open subsets <math>U</math> of <math>X</math>. In other words, <math>J</math> is a [[sheaf of modules|sheaf of {{math|''A''}}-submodules]] of <math>A</math>. <!-- What is Gamma? -->

== General properties ==

If <math>f:A\to B</math> is a homomorphism between two sheaves of rings on the same space <math>X</math>, the kernel of <math>f</math> is an ideal sheaf in <math>A</math>.

Conversely, for any ideal sheaf <math>J</math> in a sheaf of rings <math>A</math>, there is a natural structure of a sheaf of rings on the [[quotient sheaf]] <math>A/J</math>. Note that the canonical map
:<math>\Gamma(U,A)/\Gamma(U,J) \to \Gamma(U,A/J)</math>
for open subsets <math>U</math> is injective, but not surjective in general (see [[sheaf cohomology]]).

== Motivation ==

In the context of [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]], the importance of ideal sheaves lies mainly in the correspondence between closed [[subscheme]]s and [[quasi-coherent sheaf|quasi-coherent]] ideal sheaves. Consider a scheme <math>X</math> and a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf <math>J</math> in <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>. Then, the support <math>Z</math> of <math>\mathcal{O}_X/J</math> is a closed subspace of <math>X</math>, and <math>(Z,\mathcal{O}_X/J)</math> is a scheme (both assertions can be checked locally). It is called the closed subscheme of <math>X</math> defined by <math>J</math>. Conversely, let <math>i:Z\to X</math> be a [[closed immersion]], i.e., a morphism which is a [[homeomorphism]] onto a closed subspace such that the associated map
:<math>i^\# : \mathcal{O}_X\to i_*\mathcal{O}_Z</math>
is surjective on the stalks. Then, the kernel <math>J</math> of <math>i^\#</math> is a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and <math>i</math> induces an isomorphism from <math>Z</math> onto the closed subscheme defined by <math>J</math>.{{sfnp|Grothendieck|Dieudonné|1971|loc=4.2.2 (b)}}

A particular case of this correspondence is the unique [[reduced scheme|reduced]] subscheme <math>X_{\mathrm{red}}</math> of <math>X</math> having the same underlying space, which is defined by the [[Nilradical of a ring|nilradical]] of <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math> (defined stalk-wise, or on open affine charts).{{sfnp|Grothendieck|Dieudonné|1971|loc=5.1}}

For a morphism <math>f:X\to Y</math> and a closed subscheme <math>Y'\subseteq Y</math> defined by an ideal sheaf <math>J</math>, the preimage <math>Y'\times_Y X</math> is defined by the ideal sheaf{{sfnp|Grothendieck|Dieudonné|1971|loc=4.4.5}}
:<math>f^*(J)\mathcal{O}_X = \operatorname{im}(f^*J\to \mathcal{O}_X)</math>.

The pull-back of an ideal sheaf <math>J</math> to the subscheme <math>Z</math> defined by <math>J</math> contains important information, it is called the [[conormal bundle]] of <math>Z</math>. For example, the sheaf of [[Kähler differential]]s may be defined as the pull-back of the ideal sheaf defining the diagonal <math>X\to X\times X</math> to <math>X</math>. (Assume for simplicity that <math>X</math> is [[separated morphism|separated]] so that the diagonal is a closed immersion.){{sfnp|Grothendieck|1967|loc=16.1.2, 16.3.1}}

== Analytic geometry ==

In the theory of [[complex-analytic space]]s, the [[Oka-Cartan theorem]] states that a closed subset <math>A</math> of a complex space is analytic if and only if the ideal sheaf of functions vanishing on <math>A</math> is [[coherent sheaf|coherent]]. This ideal sheaf also gives <math>A</math> the structure of a reduced closed complex subspace.
